NutriGlobal Foods - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriGlobal Foods Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star, then one on your telephone keypad. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Vice President of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriGlobal Foods' Q3 results. Joining me on the call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Growth Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Elena.

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on four key areas: performance in our key channels of retail, foodservice, and convenience; updates on our M&A activity and portfolio management; our pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies; and organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter and full year.

First, regarding performance in key channels: We saw robust growth across retail, foodservice, and convenience, outpacing category averages through targeted execution and innovation in health-focused products.

Second, concerning updates on M&A and portfolio management: We've completed strategic bolt-ons and divestitures that sharpen our focus on high-growth pillars like healthy snacking and hydration.

Third, in terms of pricing actions and revenue growth management: Our disciplined approach drove meaningful contributions to top-line growth while protecting volumes.

Finally, looking at organic sales growth guidance: We're raising our outlook, reflecting confidence in our core brands and regional momentum.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to provide more detail on our financial results and expand on these areas.

Michael Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Elena. As Elena mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3. Net sales were $4.8 billion, representing an 8.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 45%, impacted by elevated input costs in commodities like cocoa and dairy but offset by pricing discipline and procurement efficiencies. Operating income was $576 million, and earnings per share were $1.28. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $2.5 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Let me now expand on the key areas Elena highlighted, starting with our performance across our three core channels—retail, foodservice, and convenience—which collectively drove that 8.2% year-over-year organic revenue growth in the quarter, outpacing the broader Food & Beverage category's 4.1% IRI-measured growth. This resilience reflects our disciplined execution amid persistent inflation pressures, supply chain normalization, and shifting consumer behaviors toward value-seeking and health-focused options.

Retail remains our largest channel at 52% of net sales, delivering 7.5% organic growth, fueled by a healthy 4.2% volume increase and 3.1% net pricing realization. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of market share gains in IRI-tracked multi-outlet universe, where we expanded to 2.1 share points in beverages and 1.3 in snacks, largely at the expense of private label erosion. Key drivers included our HydraBoost functional water line, which posted 28% YoY growth, capturing premium shelf space in high-velocity doors like Walmart and Kroger. We achieved 92% ACV distribution—up 300 basis points QoQ—through targeted resets and modular expansions, reducing out-of-stocks to under 5% via our AI-optimized replenishment partnership with Blue Yonder. In snacks, our NutriCrunch baked chips saw 15% uplift from health halo positioning, aligning with the 12% category premiumization trend per Nielsen data. Regionally, U.S. retail grew 9%, bolstered by back-to-school promotions yielding 18% household penetration lift. Europe was softer at 3% due to regulatory headwinds on HFSS reformulations, but we mitigated with 5% growth in plant-based yogurt alternatives. APAC shone at 12%, driven by e-commerce velocity in China via Tmall partnerships. Strategically, we're leaning into better-for-you innovation, with 20% of SKUs now reformulated to under 100 calories per serving, and sustainability creds like 30% recycled PET in bottles, which resonated in shopper surveys showing 15-point loyalty gains.

Foodservice, 28% of sales, accelerated to 12.4% organic growth—our strongest in two years—versus flat category performance amid labor shortages and menu price fatigue. Volume surged 6.8%, outpacing pricing at 5.2%, thanks to deep penetration in QSR and casual dining. Standouts included our QuickSip ready-to-drink coffees, up 35% YoY in McDonald's and Starbucks programs, where we secured national pours via value-engineered 16-oz formats. In institutional, school district contracts grew 22%, riding the post-COVID reimbursement tailwinds under the USDA's healthier meals mandate. Overall, we hit 85% distribution in the Technomic Foodservice Index top 500 chains, with velocity up 14% from combo meal bundling. U.S. led at 14% growth, with Texas and Florida hotspots from tourism rebound. EMEA grew 9%, offsetting UK cost pressures with LFL gains in quick-service via Greggs partnerships. Latin America lagged at 5% due to FX volatility but improved sequentially on Brazilian rodizio restaurant wins. Our playbook here emphasizes operator economics: co-branded LTOs delivered 25% trial rates, and our FlexPack portion-control pouches reduced waste by 18%, enhancing our stickiness in a channel where 40% of operators cite margin squeeze as top concern, per Datassential.

Convenience, 20% of sales, delivered standout 11.7% organic growth, triple the channel's 3.8% Nielsen c-store comps, driven by 7.1% volume and 4.3% pricing. Impulse categories like energy drinks and protein bars were engines, with our PowerPulse energy shots exploding 42% amid 24/7 snacking trends. We expanded to 88% ACV in top c-store banners—7-Eleven, Circle K, Wawa—via planogram wins and cooler door dominance, boosting facings by 15%. Out-of-stocks dropped to 3.2% through vendor-managed inventory with Core-Mark, and promo effectiveness hit 22% sales lift on buy-one-get-one-50%-off redemptions. Regionally, U.S. convenience flew at 13%, with Midwest gas station clusters leading on road-trip demand. Canada matched at 13% via Tim Hortons adjacency sales. Emerging markets like Mexico grew 16% on OXXO expansions, tapping near-universal 99% household coverage. Insights-wise, we're capitalizing on on-the-go nutrition, with 40% of new convenience SKUs fortified—e.g., 10g protein bars—aligning with the channel's 19% impulse growth in functional products. Digital tie-ins, like Circle K app exclusives, drove 30% incremental traffic.

In aggregate, these channels underscore our portfolio balance: retail provides scale, foodservice traffic, and convenience velocity. Total distribution gains of 450 bps YoY position us for FY organic growth of 7-9%, with 2-3 points from pricing discipline amid softening CPI at 3.2%. Looking ahead, we'll invest $150 million in supply chain agility—including a new aseptic filling line in Georgia for 20% capacity uplift—and double down on data analytics via our NielsenIQ and IRI symbiosis for predictive assortment. Amid economic uncertainty, our focus on affordable premium—e.g., $1.29 single-serve packs—and ESG—scopes 1-2 emissions down 12%—will sustain share in a market where consumers prioritize value 68% of the time, per Kantar.

Next, on updates to our M&A activity and portfolio management: As we continue to execute on our Nourish Forward strategy, we've remained disciplined in our capital allocation amid persistent inflation in commodity inputs like cocoa and dairy—up 12% and 8% year-over-year, respectively—and softening consumer demand in core categories. Our focus is high-conviction, bolt-on acquisitions in adjacent high-growth segments, rigorous portfolio pruning, and leveraging our $2.5 billion cash position to drive mid-single-digit organic growth while targeting 15% ROIC on deployed capital.

In late Q2, we closed our $450 million acquisition of VitaPure Snacks, a California-based leader in plant-based protein bars and functional snacks. Acquired at a compelling 9.5x trailing twelve-month EBITDA multiple, this expands our Healthy Snacking platform—which now represents 28% of our total portfolio—into the $15 billion U.S. better-for-you snacks market. VitaPure brings innovative products like almond-protein crunch bars fortified with adaptogens and 20g of plant protein per serving, aligning with the 22% CAGR in functional nutrition demand per Nielsen data. Synergies are tracking ahead of our $25 million annual run-rate target: 60% realized in procurement savings through our global supply chain, including consolidated sourcing of pea protein from North American suppliers, and 40% in G&A overlaps via SAP S/4HANA integration. Pro forma for VitaPure, Healthy Snacking delivered 14% organic revenue growth in Q3, with EBITDA margins expanding 220 basis points to 22.5%.

Complementing this, we announced and expect to close by year-end our $320 million tuck-in acquisition of EuroHydrate Beverages in EMEA. EuroHydrate's low-sugar, electrolyte-enhanced RTD beverages—like coconut water hybrids with 50% less sugar than Gatorade—bolster our Hydration & Wellness category amid the 18% YoY surge in non-alcoholic functional drinks across Europe, driven by EU front-of-pack nutrition labeling. Acquired at 8.2x EBITDA, this enhances distribution: we've secured listings in 1,200 Tesco and Carrefour stores, leveraging our Oasis juice footprint. Expected synergies of $18 million include $10 million from manufacturing optimization at shared aseptic lines in the Netherlands, reducing SKUs by 15% through formula harmonization.

Our inorganic growth pipeline includes 10-12 opportunities under diligence, values $100 million to $1 billion. About 60% target North America for health halo products like organic yogurts and keto snacks, eyeing 10% share gains vs. Chobani and Quest. APAC is 25%, prioritizing Indonesia and India for ready-to-eat meals on 9% CAGR per Euromonitor. We've passed on commodity-exposed targets like sugar confectionery due to 15-20% input inflation.

On portfolio management, we've accelerated rationalization around four pillars: Healthy Snacking, Hydration & Wellness, Plant-Powered Proteins, and Premium Convenience Foods. These now account for 72% of our $18.2 billion TTM revenue, up from 55% two years ago, with blended 16% EBITDA margins vs. 9% legacy. A key milestone was the Q3 divestiture of our North American canned pasta business—sold for $280 million, or 6.8x EBITDA. This underperformer freed proceeds for debt reduction—net leverage to 2.1x—and buybacks, yielding 150 bps ROIC uplift. We're advancing spin-off of LATAM commodity beverages by mid-2024, valued at $1.2 billion EV (7x EBITDA), crystallizing $800 million after-tax to exit low-margin exposure to FX in Brazil and Mexico.

Regionally, North America (52% revenues) doubles down on e-commerce—VitaPure up 35% Amazon velocity. EMEA (25%) gains from EuroHydrate in Aldi, offsetting UK softness. APAC (15%) prunes staples like instant noodles for premium matcha beverages. LATAM (8%) focuses plant-based post-divestiture.

We're enhancing via Nourish AI Hub: AI deal screening on 20 years F&B data, prioritizing >15% CAGR and ESG >75/100. RPA cut VitaPure ERP time 40%. All deals align Scope 3 goals—VitaPure regenerative almonds reduce water 30%. Financially, M&A/divestitures added 3.2 points to 8% growth, $42 million EBITDA accretion. Expect 200 bps margin expansion FY to 18-19%. We'll deploy $1-1.5 billion M&A/buybacks 2024, leverage <2.5x, 2.8% dividend yield. This fuels a leaner, higher-growth NutriGlobal.

Turning to pricing actions and revenue growth management—or RGM—strategies, which drove organic net revenue growth of 5.2%, with pricing contributing 6.8 points, offset by 1.1-point volume headwind and 0.5-point mix shift. In F&B, where margins face commodity volatility, input inflation, and consumer shifts, RGM is our moat.

Over 12 months, three waves of targeted increases across snacks, beverages, plant-based dairy—4-7% average—calibrated by price elasticity modeling on 15 years IRI/Nielsen data and 25 million household loyalty insights. Price-mix elasticity at -1.8, better than -2.2 target.

Snacks (42% revenues): 7.2% YoY pricing, list hikes on CrunchBar and ProteinPacks. North America 8.5% amid +25% to +12% oils/nuts inflation, elasticity -1.5 as loyalists traded up.

Beverages: 5.9%, functional waters/RTD coffees +8% on premiumization. Dynamic pricing pilots in U.S. clubs via Revionics lifted revenue per case 3.2% sans volume loss.

Plant-Based Dairy: 4.1%, offset by trade spend cut 18% to 15% via PromoRight analytics.

North America: 8.1 points, No. 2 salty snacks share per Circana, elasticity -1.6. EMEA: 3.9 points vs. Aldi/Lidl, countered by value engineering holding margins 38%, volumes +1.2%. APAC/LATAM: 5.4 points, Brazil soy milks +9% passed cleanly, -1.2 elasticity.

RGM pillars: Optimize core—SKU prune 12% of 1,200, freeing $45 million for ROI. Premiumization: 32% sales premium, 150 bps mix from VitalFuel bars (+45%), upcycled shakes. Promotion: Trade spend 16.8% vs. 19.2%, FreshRewards app 18 million users +22% repeats, blockchain pilots.

Outlook: FY organic 4-6%, pricing 5-7 points as wheat -15% QoQ, dairy +8%. Expand dynamic pricing 40% U.S., 15 NPD health launches, e-com 12%.

For organic sales growth guidance for Q4 and FY 2025: Organic reflects core on constant currency, excluding M&A/FX. Q3 5.2% beat 4.5% midpoint: 2.8% volume, 1.7% pricing, 0.7% mix. North America 6.1% on low-sugar beverages, EMEA 4.3%, APAC 3.9%, LATAM 4.8%.

Q4: 4% to 6%, lapping 7.2%. Volume 1.5-2.5% on health/wellness like plant-based dairy (12% share gains Nielsen). Pricing 1.5-2.5% as inflation mid-single. Mix 1% from RTD coffee (15% repeats). North America 5-7% e-com 18%, SKU prune 15% low-velocity. EMEA 3-5% vs. HFSS, organic tea +20%. APAC 3.5-5.5% matcha snacks +2 share. LATAM 4-6% Brazil c-stores.

FY 2025 raised to 5.5-7.5% from 5-7%: H1 6-8%, H2 5-7%. Volume 2-3% Health Forward 25 SKUs (collagen yogurt, keto kits +25% baskets). Pricing 2-3% AI model +10% elasticity. Mix 1-1.5% premium 22% refrigerated, $150B wellness 8% CAGR.

Invest $250M supply chain (almond vertical), ERP +50bps margins. Sustainability: regenerative soy -18% Scope 3, Gen Z +15% premiums. Risks: inflation/private labels, Ukraine wheat, Olipop competition. But 45% gross, 12% op margins, $2.5B liquidity.

For full year, we are raising our guidance for organic sales growth to 5.5% to 7.5%.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a headwind, particularly in commodities like edible oils, nuts, cocoa, and dairy, which have seen double-digit increases. However, our pricing discipline—averaging 6-7% across waves—and RGM strategies have more than offset this, delivering 320 basis points of gross margin expansion to 45%. We've used AI-driven elasticity models to pass through costs effectively, holding elasticity around -1.6 to -1.8, while protecting velocity through value engineering and premium mix shifts. This positions us resiliently as inflation moderates.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for the new plant-based product line and what is the expected revenue impact?

Lisa Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. Our new plant-based dairy alternatives and protein snacks are central to Health Forward, with 25 SKUs launching including collagen-enriched yogurts and keto meal kits. Early pilots mirror Danone/Kellogg trends with 25% higher basket sizes. Plant-based now 22% refrigerated portfolio, targeting $150B wellness market. We expect 2-3 points volume tailwinds FY25, plus mix uplift, contributing 1-1.5 points to organic growth. Integrations like VitaPure add 14% segment growth, with listings expanding via EuroHydrate synergies.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Raj Singh (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Thanks, David. We're investing $250M in resilience, including vertical integration in almonds to hedge droughts and a new Georgia aseptic line for 20% capacity. AI replenishment with Blue Yonder cut out-of-stocks to 3-5%, vendor-managed inventory optimizes c-stores. ERP upgrades unlock 50bps margins via turns. Regenerative programs with Argentine soy farmers reduced Scope 3 18%, RPA streamlines post-M&A. Amid disruptions, distribution +450bps YoY, positioning for agility.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Sarah Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Sarah Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Michael Chen (CFO):
Sarah, thanks. Q4 organic 4-6% sets up FY25 raise to 5.5-7.5%, with pricing 5-7 points as costs stabilize. Channels balanced: retail scale, foodservice recovery, convenience impulse. M&A pipeline robust, portfolio leaner at 72% high-growth pillars. RGM drives 4-6% FY organic, margins to 18-19%. $1-1.5B deploy M&A/buybacks, leverage <2.5x. Confident in mid-single top-line through cycle despite risks.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriGlobal Foods. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
aspects: Organic sales growth guidance for the next quarter/year
Performance in key channels: retail, foodservice, convenience
Updates on M&A activity and portfolio management
Discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies

aspect_summary.Organic sales growth guidance for the ne: Raised guidance to 4-6% organic growth for Q4 and 5.5-7.5% for FY 2025 (from prior 5-7%), reflecting confidence in core brands, health-focused innovation, and regional momentum; full year (current FY) also raised to 5.5-7.5%.
aspect_summary.Performance in key channels: retail, foo: Robust Q3 organic growth across channels driving 8.2% overall (outpacing category): Retail (52% sales) 7.5% fueled by volume and pricing in beverages/snacks; Foodservice (28%) 12.4% led by QSR/institutional; Convenience (20%) 11.7% via impulse energy/protein products; balanced portfolio with distribution gains positions for FY 7-9%.
aspect_summary.Updates on M&A activity and portfolio ma: Completed $450M VitaPure Snacks bolt-on (healthy snacking) and $280M canned pasta divestiture; $320M EuroHydrate tuck-in pending (hydration); pipeline of 10-12 deals; portfolio rationalized to four high-growth pillars (72% revenue, up from 55%); LATAM beverages spin-off by mid-2024; M&A/divestitures added 3.2 points to growth.
aspect_summary.Discussion of pricing actions and revenu: Pricing contributed 6.8 points to Q3 5.2% organic growth via three waves of 4-7% targeted increases (elasticity -1.8); RGM pillars include SKU pruning (12%), premiumization (32% sales), optimized promotions (trade spend down to 16.8%); FY pricing 5-7 points amid moderating inflation; strategies protected volumes and expanded margins.
